Design research · updated 15 August 2026 · Expo React Native · phone, iPad and desktop

Responsive authentication

Adapting premium football references and current Apple/Google identity guidance into an original, accessible Champo sign-in/sign-up flow that preserves existing Supabase behavior.

SynthesisProvider iconsInputReferencesComparisonRecommendationsExperience

Title and scope

Inference

Job: let returning users authenticate quickly and new users create a secure account with minimal ambiguity. Constraints: Hebrew/English, keyboard-safe mobile forms, existing Supabase handlers, Apple availability by platform, Google branding, and a single codebase across native and web. Success: the primary action and recovery path stay reachable at phone heights; tablet/desktop space improves focus rather than stretching fields.

Executive synthesis

Observed fact

Two distinct task hierarchies

The supplied sign-in screen prioritizes recovery and two federated providers. The sign-up screen instead prioritizes identity fields, password strength and legal consent.

Recommendation

Responsive composition, fixed form measure

Cap form width around 480–520 logical pixels. On wide canvases, add a complementary brand panel instead of widening text fields.

Recommendation

Keep persistent labels

The references correctly retain labels above filled fields. Placeholders alone disappear and are weaker for recovery, autofill and cognitive accessibility.

Inference

Hero imagery must yield to the keyboard

Large decorative art is valuable before interaction but should shrink or move aside at compact heights so fields and actions remain reachable.

Provider icon-only decision

Continue with
G
Source-reported claim

Apple explicitly permits 1:1 logo-only buttons and requires its supplied padded artwork, a black or white treatment, and a clear margin around the control.

Apple HIG · accessed 15 Aug 2026.

Equal provider prominence
Source-reported claim

Google supports icon mode, requires the multicolor G inside a recognizable button boundary, and asks that third-party providers receive comparable visual prominence.

Google branding guidelines · accessed 15 Aug 2026.

Recommendation

Champo adaptation

Place two 52×52 controls in one centered row below a localized “Continue with” label. Keep the full provider action in accessibility labels, preserve official artwork, and show a loading indicator inside the selected group without layout shift.

Inference

Risk boundary

Removing visible labels increases recognition burden. The group heading, familiar official marks, equal button treatment, and native-device validation reduce—but do not eliminate—that risk.

Patterns in production auth flows

Observed fact

Airbnb

The mobile flow uses one focused identifier step, one primary Continue action, a quiet divider and clearly grouped alternative providers. Recovery stays inside the flow instead of creating a separate visual system.

Airbnb sign-up flow reference · accessed 15 Aug 2026.

Observed fact

Strava

Strava groups Google and Apple together, separates email with a simple divider, reserves the filled brand color for the primary action and keeps account switching plus legal copy visually secondary.

Strava login · accessed 15 Aug 2026.

Observed fact

Notion

Notion presents provider methods and email in one narrow, centered surface, uses short explanatory copy and keeps terms, privacy and help available without competing with the main task.

Notion login methods · accessed 15 Aug 2026.

Observed fact

Spotify

Spotify follows a strict vertical hierarchy: provider group, divider, identifier field, one Continue action and a single account-mode switch. Decorative content does not interrupt the form.

Spotify login · accessed 15 Aug 2026.

Recommendation

Champo system rule

Use one responsive auth scaffold across sign-in, sign-up, recovery, reset and verification: fixed 520px maximum width, one surface, consistent header, persistent field labels, one gold primary action and quiet support/legal links.

Inference

Transfer boundary

The products differ in authentication methods and brand tone, so Champo adopts their hierarchy and recovery patterns—not their distinctive composition, copy or visual identity.

Input analysis

Observed fact

Shared structure

Back action, centered wordmark, stadium atmosphere, strong headline, supporting copy, outlined fields, gold primary button and a mode-switching text link.

Observed fact

Sign-up-specific

Shield illustration, name/email/password, four-part strength meter, legal checkbox, create-account CTA, then sign-in link. No federated buttons are shown.

Observed fact

Sign-in-specific

Email/password, trailing field icons, password recovery, sign-in CTA, divider, Apple and Google actions, then registration link.

Recommendation

Adaptation boundary

Use the existing stadium artwork and native controls; replace the distinctive shield illustration with a simpler local trust emblem and do not encode any localized text in imagery.

Top references

Limitation Official guidance was available, but complete live signed-out flows and downloadable product screenshots were not. Original schematics below represent guidance structure, not copied product screens.

Apple · Sign in with AppleContinue with Apple
Source-reported claim

Apple says its authentication can let people skip forms, email verification and password creation, and recommends explaining why sign-in benefits them.

Apple HIG · accessed 6 Aug 2026.

Google IdentityContinue with Google
Source-reported claim

Google requires the standard multicolor G, localized action text, preserved proportions and prominence comparable to other third-party providers.

Google branding guidelines · accessed 6 Aug 2026.

Apple · Text fieldsSubmit
Source-reported claim

Apple recommends hints plus persistent labels when useful, secure password entry, and purpose icons at the leading edge with actions at the trailing edge.

Apple HIG text fields · accessed 6 Aug 2026.

Apple · Adaptive layoutFull layout until it no longer fits
Source-reported claim

Apple advises adapting dynamically to display traits and keeping a full layout until it no longer fits, rather than defining layouts only by device names.

Apple HIG layout · accessed 6 Aug 2026.

W3C · Input purposeAutofill-friendly
Source-reported claim

WCAG guidance asks that common input purposes be programmatically identifiable, supporting autofill and alternative presentations.

W3C SC 1.3.5 · accessed 6 Aug 2026.

W3C · Accessible authenticationPasswords + assisted alternatives
Source-reported claim

WCAG 2.2 permits password authentication when mechanisms such as password managers and copy/paste assist the user; it also highlights adequate target size.

WCAG 2.2 · accessed 6 Aug 2026.

What leaders do differently

Recommendation

Platform-trusted identity

Provider buttons should remain recognizable and semantically equal; Champo's gold CTA stays reserved for email/password submission.

Recommendation

Help at the point of need

Password recovery belongs next to password entry, while sign-up strength requirements should update before submission.

Inference

Large screens reduce distraction

A split layout can preserve atmosphere while keeping the form compact. Stretching a single mobile column would reduce scan efficiency.

Fast, low-friction first run

DimensionDecisionReason
Time to valueTwo fields to sign in; three to sign upNo unrelated profile setup
DecisionsEmail flow or provider on sign-inAlternatives appear after the primary action
PermissionsNoneAuthentication does not require notification/location access
DefaultsCorrect keyboard/autofill purposesReduces typing and error burden
RecoveryForgot password remains visibleSupports returning users without dead ends
TrustLegal links and consent before account creationConsent is specific and reviewable

Risks and anti-patterns

Recommendation

Do not place labels only inside fields

Filled inputs must retain their identity, especially with autofill and RTL.

Recommendation

Do not make desktop fields full width

Cap the interactive measure and use space for supporting imagery or calm whitespace.

Recommendation

Do not hide actions behind the keyboard

Allow vertical scrolling and preserve focused-input visibility.

Recommendation

Do not imitate provider logos

Keep the official Google mark and Apple-generated logo-only artwork while preserving native Apple authentication.

Recommendations

P0 · Medium effort · High confidence

Recommendation

Responsive auth shell

Mobile stack below 900px; wide split composition at 900px+; compact vertical mode below about 720px height.

Validate: 390×667, 390×844, 768×1024 and 1440×900.

P0 · Medium effort · High confidence

Recommendation

Persistent labeled fields

Extend the shared field API with labels and visual variants instead of creating inaccessible one-off inputs.

Validate: empty, filled, focused, invalid, disabled and autofilled states.

P0 · Low effort · High confidence

Recommendation

Mode-specific content

Show social providers on sign-in; show password meter and explicit consent on sign-up.

Validate: route starts in the requested mode and switches without stale errors.

P1 · Low effort · Medium confidence

Recommendation

Trust emblem

Use a simple local shield/check composition, scaled down or omitted in compact height.

Validate: it never pushes fields below the first viewport on small phones.

Proposed experience

Recommendation

Responsive states

Phone: compact logo/header, form, scroll as needed. Tablet portrait: centered card with wider margins and restrained hero. Tablet landscape/desktop: two columns—visual brand story and max-width form card. Keyboard: visual region collapses and focused input remains visible.

Components

`ResponsiveAuthShell`, shared wordmark, trust emblem, labeled `InputField`, password-strength meter, consent row, primary gold action, provider group and mode-switch footer.

Accessibility

Persistent labels, programmatic input purposes, 48–56pt controls, visible focus treatment on web, error text associated with its field, password visibility label/state, no color-only strength signal, and RTL-aware icon placement.

Analytics

Future events may include auth mode shown, submit attempted, validation category, provider selected and recovery selected; do not record emails, names, passwords or error payloads containing personal data.

Sources and limitations

Observed fact

The two supplied screenshots and local implementation were inspected without uploading them externally.

Source-reported claim

Platform and accessibility guidance comes from the linked Apple, Google and W3C primary sources, accessed 6 August 2026.

Limitation

No behavioral study of Champo users was available, and comparator product authentication flows may vary by platform, locale, release or experiment. Recommendations should be validated on real devices and with Hebrew users.

Self-contained report. Supplied inputs are embedded; diagrams are original local schematics; sources are linked for attribution.
